narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

Slightly cooler and clearer than yesterday; winds little changed. Showers reported at Kisumu International Airport as of 04:00, with thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening. 30°C / 86°F high, 20°C / 67°F low. Sky mostly cloudy early as reported, partly cloudy at midday and mostly cloudy in the evening. Wind N early and SW at midday; gusts to 37 km/h (20 kt). UV index 9.3 (very high). Air quality 52 (moderate) at Dunga Beach, the highest of 3 stations. As of 06:01, reports through 04:00: rain from 00:00; no thunder; high so far 21°C / 70°F; low so far 21°C / 70°F; peak sustained 15 km/h; sky mostly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS: temperatures and winds much the same through Thursday, with rain and thunderstorms likely each day. Tuesday will be Mostly cloudy with rain 3.1–21.3 mm, high 28–32 °C, gusts to 30 km/h (16 kt). Wednesday Mostly cloudy, rain 4.9–11.7 mm, high 28–31 °C, gusts to 27 km/h (14 kt). Thursday Mostly cloudy, rain 8.1–30.1 mm, high 27–31 °C, gusts to 24 km/h (13 kt). The Day+3 call gives a high range of 27–31 °C and the Day+7 call a high range of 27–29 °C. RECORD: best rain record GFS for today, ECMWF for Day+3 and Day+7.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values exceed the thunderstorm threshold, with the Best Match, ECMWF, ICON and UKMO models indicating strong instability and a peak at 19:00. This supports the forecast of thunder possible from the morning, peaking this evening, and suggests gusts could surge well above the 37 km/h (20 kt) forecast wind. No specific bulletin from the Kenya Meteorological Department warns of severe weather at this time.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

Over Winam Gulf the wind is overnight at 6 km/h (3 kt) gusting 11 km/h (6 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 17 km/h (9 kt), and into the evening at 10 km/h (5 kt) gusting 20 km/h (11 kt); peak gust 25 km/h (13 kt). Thunderstorm gust hazard remains possible as thunder is possible from the morning, peaking this evening.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1008 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1015 hPa) – a moderate large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the north is filling over the next three days. Pressure is also falling toward the south, southeast, southwest, though the speed of approach is unknown. Pressure overhead is near-steady. BASIN PRESSURE: today’s mean sea-level pressure sits between 1013.5 and 1015.5 hPa; near-steady over three days (-0.5 hPa). The trend is +0.5 hPa.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

REVIEW notes that at Day+0 no model is meaningfully better than the others, and that Best Match slightly under-forecasts peak wind. The call’s peak gust of 37 km/h (20 kt) sits between GFS’s 14.4 km/h and Best Match’s 34.9 km/h, reflecting the spread. ECMWF’s rain probability is high (83 %) and its CAPE is 1680 J/kg, but its peak wind is under-forecast, matching the review comment. The GFS model records the best rain verification for today, while ECMWF holds the best rain record for Day+3 and Day+7. KMD’s own forecast aligns with the call on temperature and rain likelihood, though it lacks a detailed wind estimate. DATA SUFFICIENCY shows 56 checks for Day+0, providing a settled picture despite uneven KMD coverage.
